abstract: Language models are known to encode simple relations, such as synonymy, in the geometry of their representations. It is unclear whether they also encode complex patterns of relationships such as those that drive analogy. We present a simple method, with no learned parameters, based on comparing the internal structural arrangements between disparate domains, to test this. Using our method we find over multiple models that representations are arranged consistently to encode complex relationship similarities. Models align distant representation clouds so that facets of meaning are easily comparable under simple mappings. Our work extends mechanistic accounts of representation space to the relative arrangement of representations that may be only weakly related to one another, showing that representation geometry is far richer than previously thought. Code and data: https://github.com/lcowley7/embedded_relationships
